chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Hartford doctors send him home and Dr. Mayer takes over again
summary: Refusing amputation, Cobb is sent home by ambulance, stays in bed through the summer, then enters Hospital for Joint Disease under Dr. Mayer from October 1956 to January 1957.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, so what kind -- who was the doctor that treated you for your legs then in those three months?
At Hartford?
Yeah.
Well, whoever the staff doctors were there. They -- I didn't know anybody by name there.
Well, did they start you on therapy
then?

No, they did not. They told me that they may have to take this leg because it wasn't forming calcium as fast as this one. So I told them that let me live with it a little longer and let me give it a chance because I wasn't going to let them take nothing. So they got a little indignant, I guess, about it because I wouldn't let them do it, and about three days later they told me they'd done everything they could do. They would have to send me home. I said, 'Very good.'

So I asked for -- the nurse called my wife, and they had an ambulance from Englewood, New Jersey, come and pick me up. I had to go home in the ambulance. And I went home and I stayed -- this was in -- let me see -- April -- May, June, July. I went home in July and stayed in bed at home until October. Then I went back under Dr. Mayer, at the Hospital for Joint Disease, and he did the rest of it.
You went back to Dr. Mayer?
Sure, that was my doctor in New York.
This was six or seven years later.

Sure. I called him up from home and told him what was happening. And I was on a double spike that they put me in. He took me to (inaudible) hospital and put me in a double spike, [my arm] to my ankle, and they didn't split this one. It was full and all the way around.
I used to sit up (on inaudible) my chest on the case (inaudible).
How long did Dr. Mayer treat you then?
I went in October and came out January the 12th, one day after her birthday.
You mean you went back in the hospital in 1957 by then?
And come out in '57.
For another three months --
Yeah.
-- or four months.
